reviews.content:
Before I started reading this book, my son was a terrible sleeper, both day and night. I was so sleep deprived being woken anywhere from 5-10 times a night! Sometimes I just lost count! 



I had had 10 months of this and needed a break. I didn't want to let my baby cry it out. Yes I did try it once or twice against my better judgement and it only made things worse. I then heard about this book and rushed out to get it. Elizabeth writes in such an easy to understand way having gone through all this herself. The tables showing how much sleep a baby should be getting along with our own sleep logs made me realise how much sleep he (and ME!) was lacking. Another problem I had was trying to settle him without a comfort feed and him only going back to sleep on the boob. Her techniques helped us break that sleep association with perseverance. The sample routines helped show me I was on the right track and was also helpful to have ideas when his routine naturally changed and I started dropping milk feeds throughout the day. I starting seeing improvements within weeks and within 2 months he was sleeping through most nights or at least able to resettle himself should he stir. This book was such a great help to me going back to work, finally being able to get more sleep and not waking up like a zombie to go to work. My little boy is now 18 months old and only needs help to resettle through the night when he is sick. This is a purchase you will not regret!

reviews.content:
This book has really help my baby sleep though the night -and I'm finally enjoying motherhood! I read the book while I was desperately trying to get my baby to sleep (one arm holding my baby, the other trying to keep the covers open!). It took some time, but some of the given tips eventually worked out. My baby is almost 8 months old and she has learned to fall back to sleep on her own, and her dad and me are sleeping through the night.
What I like the most about TNCSS is that it doesn't offer a single ""magical"" plan. It offers you a bunch of useful tips from which you can select what best works for you, your baby and your family.
Elizabeth is not a doctor, she's a mother who understands what we are going through. While reading her book, I felt as if I was talking to a more experienced friend with a warm cup of coffee, and as she gave me the tips I though ""hey, this might actually work, let's give it a shot shall we?"".
Thank you very much, Elizabeth!

reviews.content: You need this book! As a first time mom, I read alot of books, probably too many. I should have just read this one. Pantley's ""the no-cry sleep solution"" is fantastic. It is written as a parent to parent conversation, gentle, and without judgment. Regardless of your parenting style, you will find this book helpful. It is written in a logical step-by-step approach, and is very upfront that this is a process and it will take time, but the end result is a transition that is gentle and loving - for everyone. It is well organized and clearly flags tips and tricks and who they might best suit (everyone, breastfeeders, bottle feeders, co-sleepers, etc. ). The sleep diary log sheets are very easy to use or modify. In a time where I have lacked confidence and have felt judged by the decisions I have made, this book was a welcome addition to our household. It sits by the couch and the pages are ear marked. Many of them. Get the book.

reviews.content:
This book has made a huge difference in our home and the way we sleep. My son is 7 months old and was waking 7 to 8 times a night still. The only way I could get him back to sleep was through breastfeeding - EVERY time he woke up. He began sleeping in my bed because I couldn't stay awake and feed him that many times a night and still get up and function for work in the morning.
One weekend, I read The No-Cry Sleep Solution. I was pleased to find in the book there were solutions for all kinds of families; families that breastfed or bottlefed, co-slept or didn't, and anything in between. This book offered SO MUCH advice and support. It provided lots of things you could do to help your baby sleep better without making one drastic change that is tough on you and baby. 
Ms. Pantley's book offers a way to help your little one sleep without using cry it out methods. We started on a Monday with, what I considered, small changes and by Thursday we were seeing results. My son went from waking 7 to 8 times a night to only waking 2 times!! It was amazing. If your little one is having trouble going to sleep, staying a sleep, or getting back to sleep - read this book. It will help you.
